experiment: BC5 — the black-copper boundary as an infrared rectenna: transverse IR (chi~90 deg) -> longitudinal DC current (chi->0) without high photon energy
idea: Author: the conversion needs an angle change, not energy (as in electricity, radio antennas, gravitational-wave detection). Engineering form: nanostructure = antenna array (coherent pickup), Cu/CuO junction = diode (direction), store->cold side = temperature difference (net flow).

model.per_antenna_input: single-mode (one polarization) net thermal power from store T_h to rectenna at T_c: integral of h nu/(exp(h nu/kT)-1) over nu, (T_h spectrum minus T_c spectrum), weighted by absorptance 0.96 and RC roll-off 1/(1+(nu/f_c)^2)
model.array: antennas tile the surface; covered net flux per m^2 = 0.96 sigma (T_h^4 - T_c^4) x (power fraction passed by the roll-off)
model.rectifier: small-signal square-law diode at zero bias: I_dc = beta P_in; matched load; eta_rect = beta^2 P_in R_d / 4 (capped at the Carnot factor)

predictions.P1_isothermal_zero: T_h = T_c gives zero DC output (a diode cannot rectify its own thermal noise; second law)
predictions.P2_cutoff: at T_h = 340 K a diode with f_c = 1 THz passes < 5% of the net spectral power, f_c = 30 THz passes > 50%
predictions.P3_small_signal: per-antenna input at 340 K is < 1e-7 W, so eta_rect < 1e-3 for every declared diode: the small-signal diode, not the photon energy, is the bottleneck
predictions.P4_beats_photoemission: best declared rectenna at 340 K (beta 5, R 1000, f_c 100 THz) outputs >= 100x the BC2 ideal internal-photoemission bound (6.4e-6 W/m^2)
predictions.P5_hot_store: at T_h = 773 K the best declared rectenna exceeds 1 W/m^2
